第 60 章 On the Elusiveness of Time in Tracking Progress论时间在追踪进度中的虚幻性

Mathias Meyer / 马蒂亚斯·迈耶

— 第 173 页 —

When I started my very first job out of university, I was assigned to a project that already had a predefined list of tasks and estimates. None of these I had been involved in setting. At the end of every week I sent my manager a progress report, stating how many hours I had worked on a task from the project plan and how much longer I thought it would take to finish that task. Everything was okay as long as I sent back numbers that exactly aligned with the plan.

当我大学毕业后开始第一份工作时，我被分配到一个已经有预定义任务列表和估算的项目。这些我都没参与设定。每周结束时我给经理发进度报告，说明我在项目计划的一个任务上花了多少小时、我觉得还需要多久完成。只要我发回的数字和计划完全一致就一切都好。

Engineers know from experience that estimates tend to be used as targets rather than guesses. They tend to be set in stone after they're established. And yet we also know that things tend to take longer than we expect them to. As humans we err toward optimistic estimates. Yet as managers, many of us tend to fall back to the same pattern. We look at time spent working or how long someone was in the office as our means of measuring progress.

工程师从经验知道，估算往往被当作目标而不是猜测。它们一旦建立就往往被定死。然而我们也知道事情往往比我们预期的更久。作为人类我们偏向乐观估算。然而作为经理，我们很多人倾向于回到同一个模式。我们看工作花的时间或某人在办公室待了多久作为衡量进度的方式。

Time is easy to reason about. Based on an estimate and time spent on a project so far, we can come up with a specific number of how much time we're going to spend until it's finished. The assumption then holds that when the time was used up, the project or task will be done. This is a mistake that I'm seeing many managers make, especially when they're new to management. Another mistake they tend to make is thinking that if your engineers do work more hours, you'll still achieve the goal. This might work in the short term, but in the long term, you'll burn out your team. They'll end up leaving the company if things don't improve, if you don't improve. Working overtime is a short-term fix, and it should be a last resort. Otherwise, it's damaging not just to your organization, it's damaging to your people.

时间很容易推理。基于估算和到目前为止在项目上花的时间，我们可以算出到完成还要花多少时间的具体数字。然后假设时间用完时项目或任务就完成了。这是我看到很多经理犯的错误，尤其是新经理。他们倾向犯的另一个错误是认为如果工程师工作更多小时，你仍然会实现目标。短期可能有效，但长期你会让团队倦怠。如果事情不改善、你不改善，他们最终会离开公司。加班是短期修复，应该是最后手段。否则它不仅损害组织，也损害你的人。

— 第 174 页 —

Measuring progress in time is a focus on output. It's similar to lines of code. It tells you that work might have been done, or rather that time has passed that you expect was spent productively and exclusively working on that task. This is rarely the reality. Meetings, impromptu conversations, changing priorities, and unplanned work tend to creep up on engineers all the time. It's not an inherently bad thing that they do, it just happens. Writing code is an inherently creative activity. It requires thinking about a problem, building prototypes to verify assumptions, and adjusting course when those assumptions aren't met. Experienced engineers learn how to get their estimates closer and closer to reality. But as humans, we fall on the side of being too optimistic when it comes to predicting the future and guessing how long something is going to take.

用时间衡量进度是聚焦输出。它类似于代码行数。它告诉你工作可能完成了，或者说时间过去了，你期望那是富有成效地、专门花在那个任务上的。这很少是现实。会议、即兴对话、改变的优先级、计划外工作总是悄悄找上工程师。它们做的事本身不是坏事，只是发生。写代码本质上是创造性活动。它需要思考问题、建原型验证假设、当假设不成立时调整方向。有经验的工程师学习怎么让估算越来越接近现实。但作为人类，我们在预测未来、猜测某事要多久时偏向过于乐观。

How do you get past using time as the sole indicator of progress? How can you make sure, as the manager, that you're on top of your team's progress? The most difficult activity you'll need to do with your team is to break down the work. For any project, no matter how long, be deliberate about breaking the work down into smaller pieces. Allow your team to verify assumptions quickly and have a regular discussion about progress.

你怎么超越把时间作为进度唯一指标？作为经理你怎么确保掌握团队进度？你需要和团队做的最困难的活动是拆解工作。对任何项目，无论多长，都要有意把工作拆成更小的块。让团队快速验证假设，定期讨论进度。

For each week, set goals with your team of what they'd like to achieve. Check in with them in the middle of the week on how confident they are as to whether they're going to reach those goals. A 1-to-10 scale is sufficient, unless you're German or Swiss; in which case, go for 0 to 100%. If they're not confident, ask them why and adjust as needed. At the end of each week, review your progress. Did you achieve your goals? If so, keep going! If not, what got in the way? Were those goals too optimistic? Adjust your goals for the next weeks based on what you've learned. Repeat this every week.

每周和团队设定他们想达成的目标。周中时检查他们对能否达成目标有多少信心。1-10 分足够，除非你是德国人或瑞士人；那样就用 0-100%。如果他们没信心，问为什么并按需调整。每周结束时回顾进度。你达成目标了吗？如果是，继续！如果没有，是什么挡了路？那些目标太乐观了吗？根据学到的东西调整下周目标。每周重复。

As time is an unavoidable part of working in a business, keep in mind that there are two more knobs available to you as a manager: quality and scope. If time is a fixed variable—for instance, a fixed launch date—be diligent and ruthless to cut down scope or to adjust quality as much as is bearable for the business and your team. Even though your customers and stakeholders like to say that neither quality nor scope are negotiable, they always are. It's your task as a manager to do everything you can to negotiate on them.

时间是工作中不可避免的部分，请记住作为经理你还有两个旋钮：质量和范围。如果时间是固定变量——比如固定发布日期——勤勉无情地削减范围或调整质量到业务和团队可承受的程度。即使你的客户和利益相关者喜欢说质量和范围都不可谈判，它们总是可谈判的。作为经理你的任务是尽你所能就它们谈判。
